info.title: Subsystem
info.description: RESTful interface for AOS-CX switch software

acl_init_status.description: This enum is used to represent the initialization status of a line card subsystem from the ACL feature perspective. 'none':    subsystem is still initializing. 'success': ACL is successfully applied on            the line card subsystem during initialization or            there is no ACL on the line card subsystem. 'failure': ACL is not successfully applied            on the line card subsystem during initialization.

admin_state.description: User configurable admin state of the subsystem. Valid values are:  + __diagnostic__:   Put the subsystem into diagnostic mode. + __down__:   Disable/power down the subsystem. + __up__:   Enable/power on the subsystem.

airflow_direction.description: Type of system airflow. Valid values are: F2B: Front to Back B2F: Back to Front

bist_passed.description: BIST test result: `true`   : Early BIST passed. `false`  : Early BIST failed.

reason.description: Boot reason history. Management module role active, standby subsystem types to store the last 4 reboot reasons and line card subsystem type to store the last 6 reboot reasons. Applicable to management module and line card subsystem types only. In VSF stack conductor, standby and members to store the last 4 reboot reasons.

timestamp.description: The timestamp for each boot-reason, represented in human readable format.

capacities.description: This specifies the set of capacities.

psu_slots.description: Number of power supply slots in a system.

redundant_fantrays.description: Number of fan trays in a system that can be lost and not considered as fault: 0 = No fan tray redundancy 1 = N+1 fan tray redundancy 2 = N+2 fan tray redundancy and so on

control_plane_target_state.description: Defines the state of the data plane control state machine Valid values are: `undetermined`:    Management module state unknown or unnassigned role `not_ready`:       Management module role active and in ready state.                     All associated data planes in 'absent' state `running_active`:  Management module role active and in ready state.                     Any associated data plane in 'steady' state `reconfigure_port`:Management module role reconfigure for split port reconfiguration. `insert_remove`:   Any associated data plane updating connections.                     On state 'connect', 'disconnecting' or 'first_run' `running_standby`: Management module role standby and device ready `failover`:        Management infrastructure ready for failover

data_plane_connectivity_state.description:
Reference Resource: [Subsystem](#/Subsystem)
Current connection state of the referenced subsystem's row. Valid values are: `connected`: Subsystem is connected with referencer subsystem. `disconnected`: Subsystem is not connected with referencer subsystem. `error`: Connection of referenced subsystem to referencer in failure condition.

data_plane_connectivity_target_state.description:
Reference Resource: [Subsystem](#/Subsystem)
Identifies the state of the target data plane's connection to the referenced data plane. Valid values are: `connect`: Referencer subsystem is being connected with referenced subsystem. `disconnect`: Referencer subsystem is not connected with referenced subsystem. `ready`: Referencer subsystem is connected with the referenced subsystem. `error`: Connection of referenced subsystem to referencer in failure condition.

data_plane_error.description: Describes the data plane error reason and its state before  transitioning to failure. This field is empty by default and it is only set when an error  occurs during execution.

pre_error_state.description: The state of the data plane before transitioning to the error state. See `data_plane_state' for the set of possible values.

interface_group_speed.description: The allowed link speeds configuration for each interface group of a  subsystem.    Interface groups are blocks of ports for which only a subset of link  speeds are usable at the same time due to hardware limitations. For  example, a group of ports might support 10 Gbps and 25 Gbps  transceivers, but not at the same time. When configured for `25g`,  any ports in the group with a 10 Gbps transceiver inserted cannot  link.    Groups are configured with a name describing a subset of link  speeds. The speeds allowed by each name are defined by  `interface_group_info`. Groups with no configuration default to the  name defined in `interface_group_default_speed`. The currently  applied name is available in `interface_group_applied_speed`.    Note that not all defined group and speed names are available on all  subsystems. Only groups and speeds listed in `interface_group_info`  are used on a given subsystem. Any configured groups not listed are  not used by the subsystem and are ignored. Groups configured with a  speed setting that is not valid for the subsystem use the default  instead.

interface_group_applied_speed.description: The applied speed setting for each interface group used by this  subsystem.

interface_group_default_speed.description: The default speed setting for each interface group that does not  have a value configured in `interface_group_speed`. Note that not  all defined group and speed names are used on all subsystems. Only  groups and speeds listed in `interface_group_info` are used on a  given subsystem.

interface_group_info.description: The set of link speeds that are valid for each interface group speed  setting. The values are comma-separated lists of speeds in megabits  per second, for example, `10000,25000`. Note that not all defined  group and speed names are available on all subsystems.

interface_group_speed.description: The allowed link speeds configuration for each interface group of a  subsystem.    Interface groups are blocks of ports for which only a subset of link  speeds are usable at the same time due to hardware limitations. For  example, a group of ports might support 10 Gbps and 25 Gbps  transceivers, but not at the same time. When configured for `25g`,  any ports in the group with a 10 Gbps transceiver inserted cannot  link.    Groups are configured with a name describing a subset of link  speeds. The speeds allowed by each name are defined by  `interface_group_info`. Groups with no configuration default to the  name defined in `interface_group_default_speed`. The currently  applied name is available in `interface_group_applied_speed`.    Note that not all defined group and speed names are available on all  subsystems. Only groups and speeds listed in `interface_group_info`  are used on a given subsystem. Any configured groups not listed are  not used by the subsystem and are ignored. Groups configured with a  speed setting that is not valid for the subsystem use the default  instead.

part_number_cfg.description: User configurable part number for the subsystem.  When this column is empty:  + The subsystem is not explicitly configured yet and any compatible, supported subsystem is allowed to boot. + If an existing subsystem is physically replaced with a subsystem of a different part number, the interfaces associated with the existing subsystem will be removed prior to adding interfaces of the newly inserted subsystem.  When this column is configured with a part number:  + The subsystem is explicitly configured to only allow a subsystem with that specific part number to boot. + Physically replacing the existing subsystem with a subsystem of a different part number will require adjusting this column to match the new subsystem. thermal_state.description: Temperature status of this subsystem: 'safe':     Normal operating temperature conditions.  All sensors             associated with this subsystem are within nominal             range. 'nodata':   Subsystem is initializing and awaiting temperature             state or there is no temperature data acquired for             the subsystem.  This is the default value set during             initialization. 'emergency': Temperature has reached a critical level that will              result in a hardware shutdown. 'critical': Temperature has reached a critical level and it is             recommended to take an immediate action. 'overtemp': Temperature has reached an over temperature condition             and it is recommended to take action if the             temperature does not return to the safe operating             conditions after a time.  The amount of time is             dependent upon the HW configuration. 'low':      Temperature has reached a low temperature condition             and it is recommended to take action if the             temperature does not return to the safe operating             conditions after a time.  The amount of time is             dependent upon the HW configuration. 'crit_low': Temperature has reached a low critical level and it             is recommended to take an immediate action. 'low_emergency': Temperature has reach a low critical level that will                  result in a hardware shutdown. Indicates whether the subsystem is within normal operating temperature ranges or if an action is required to prevent damage to the HW.

interface_group_speed.description: The allowed link speeds configuration for each interface group of a  subsystem.    Interface groups are blocks of ports for which only a subset of link  speeds are usable at the same time due to hardware limitations. For  example, a group of ports might support 10 Gbps and 25 Gbps  transceivers, but not at the same time. When configured for `25g`,  any ports in the group with a 10 Gbps transceiver inserted cannot  link.    Groups are configured with a name describing a subset of link  speeds. The speeds allowed by each name are defined by  `interface_group_info`. Groups with no configuration default to the  name defined in `interface_group_default_speed`. The currently  applied name is available in `interface_group_applied_speed`.    Note that not all defined group and speed names are available on all  subsystems. Only groups and speeds listed in `interface_group_info`  are used on a given subsystem. Any configured groups not listed are  not used by the subsystem and are ignored. Groups configured with a  speed setting that is not valid for the subsystem use the default  instead.
